<issue>
XML parsing fails when string starts with '<?xml'

#### Description

When parsing XML strings that start with '<?xml', the parser incorrectly strips the first 5 characters, causing malformed XML and parsing errors.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from docx.oxml.parser import parse_xml

# This should work but fails
xml_with_declaration = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="yes"?><foo><bar>test</bar></foo>'
parse_xml(xml_with_declaration)
```

The above code raises an error because the parser removes the first 5 characters ('<?xml') from any string starting with '<?xml', resulting in malformed XML like ` version="1.0" standalone="yes"?><foo><bar>test</bar></foo>`.

#### Expected Behavior

XML strings with proper XML declarations should parse correctly without modification.

#### Actual Behavior

The parser strips the first 5 characters from any string starting with '<?xml', breaking valid XML declarations and causing parsing failures.
</issue>
